title: Nissequogue / Wissiquack River
summary: Wissiquack is recorded as a corrupted form of Nissequogue in Smithtown and belongs with the Tackan/Nissequogue discussion.
history_content: The Wissiquack form appears in an early eighteenth-century petition for a survey on the north side of Suffolk County. It is part of the Nissequogue River placename history.
translation_content:
No separate translation is given for Wissiquack because it is treated as a corrupted form of Nissequogue. The Nissequogue interpretation should be reviewed with the related Tackan/Nissequogue entry.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names may be said to represent the oldest living part of human cultural heritage, in the sense that they have been handed down orally from generation to generation for hundreds or even thousands of years.”

— Botolv Helleland, Toponymy and Cultural Heritage (n.d.), ICA Course on Toponymy, introduction

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
preservation_content: The variant form remains searchable while the history stays tied to the Nissequogue River rather than becoming a separate place.
whereintheworld_content: Approximate blue/general placement along the Nissequogue River in Smithtown. Coordinates are a modern anchor and not exact survey boundaries.
